sources.title: Park Ridge Public Library Local History
sources.access_notes: Full-text Park Ridge newspapers searchable in-library only. Coverage: Park Ridge Advocate, Park Ridge Herald, Park Ridge Herald-Advocate, 1929-1935 and 1937-2023, scraps of Park Ridge Herald 1889-1923. Also holds microfilm for Herald, Times Herald, Advocate, Herald-Advocate.

sources.title: Comprehensive Plan, City of Park Ridge
sources.access_notes: 1996 document. References 1920s building boom, farm-to-subdivision transitions, nursery/greenhouse origins of subdivisions, postwar housing demand.

sources.title: Agenda Cover Memorandum, Special Service Area No. 22-104 Stewart/Crescent
sources.access_notes: References Lots 7-17 and 18-23, Block 1, Dale, Gustin and Wallace Addition to Park Ridge. Plat recorded October 1, 1873, Document No. 128686. Located in NE 1/4 Section 35, Township 41 North, Range 12 East. Related addresses: South Prospect, Courtland, Stewart, Crescent area.

sources.title: Agenda Cover Memo, 36 Main Street Special Use
sources.access_notes: 36 Main Street is Lot 2, Block 5, L. Hodge's Addition to Park Ridge. East Half of Section 35, Township 41 North, Range 12 East.

sources.title: Agenda Cover Memorandum, 110 South Prospect Avenue
sources.access_notes: 110 South Prospect Avenue is Lot 1 and Lot 2, Block 1, L. Hodge's Addition to Park Ridge.

sources.title: Park Ridge Approves Historical Survey For 'The Pretzel' Neighborhood
sources.access_notes: Reports city approval of historical survey for 'The Pretzel' neighborhood, described as about 250 lots in the L. Hodges Addition neighborhood. Known for curving streets.

sources.title: Agenda Cover Memorandum, L. Hodges Addition Intensive Historic Survey
sources.access_notes: City procured technical architectural support for Intensive Historic Survey of L. Hodges Addition. Neighborhood locally known as 'The Pretzel.'

sources.title: The History of Park Ridge, 1841-1926
sources.access_notes: Describes early Park Ridge as formerly Pennyville and Brickton. References 66x150 foot lot on Park Avenue in Root Subdivision for Catholic church. Early infrastructure: wells, plank sidewalks, limited sewer/water. Extract exact page numbers before public use.

sources.title: Cook County Municipal Incorporation and Annexation Index Document 15725727
sources.access_notes: References territory annexed to City of Park Ridge by ordinance adopted September 8, 1953. Names Zelowsky's Park Ridge Subdivision and Feuerborn and Klode's Center Street Addition.

sources.title: Agenda Cover Memorandum, Feuerborn and Klode's Ridgewood Park Subdivision
sources.access_notes: References Feuerborn and Klode's Ridgewood Park Subdivision, recorded January 13, 1925. Document number in source OCR text appears as '8737h25' - needs manual verification before public display.
